title: Thermodynamic Analysis of a Flash Tank
content: A two-phase thermodynamic model of a flash tank (FT) is proposed to predict the dy-namics of a flash tank operating with a pure substance. The model is based on the mass and energy balance equations applied to the liquid and vapor phases. It consists of five different cases related to both tank pressure changes and thermodynamic conditions of the two phases. This permits us to consider the spontaneous condensation of part of the vapor resident in the tank and/or spontaneous flashing of a fraction of resident liquid. Once the FT inlet total mass flow rate is assigned, the ones of incoming flash vapor and saturated liquid are computed as a function of the time-dependent tank pressure. A pro-cedure for computing the liquid level inside the tank is also given. As numerical tests, the thermodynamic model is applied first to a flash tank used for steam generation (powered by high temperature heat pumps or low temperature solar collectors), and then to the transient operating of a flash tank vapor injection system for a vapor-compression heat pump.
